node_definition.done_when: Read sections 1 and 3 of a-finished-worktree-releases-without-a-force first; §1 is the root cause and the census behind it. Releasing a worktree whose commits are integrated into the integration head first saves any residue: tracked-file changes as a patch, untracked files as a tar. They go into the run's directory, or for a worktree with no run into ~/.config/reckon/crew/worktree-residue/, named for the worktree. Release then removes the worktree. It first verifies that the patch applies cleanly to the worktree's head, and it prints the residue paths. Each dirty path is classified, and the class written beside the patch: subsumed (its working content equals that path at the integration head, or its change is identical to one in another preserved residue), superseded (the path also changed on the integration head since the worktree's base), or unique. A worktree whose residue includes unique source changes is preserved and released the same way, and is listed in a residue report. A worktree claimed by a live run is never touched. reckon crew gc --apply performs this release for dirty integrated worktrees, so the worktree-held obligation's existing remedy, crew gc --apply, now clears it; reckon/crew/obligations.py is not part of this node. tests/test_finished_worktree_saves_residue.py drives each class and the live-claim exclusion in a temporary repository and RECKON_HOME, and asserts that the patch round-trips and the worktree is gone. Existing gc and promotion tests (tests/test_crew_gc.py, tests/test_gc_applies_past_a_vanished_worktree.py, tests/test_gc_covers_run_directory_trees.py, tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py) keep passing; one that asserts a dirty worktree is retained is updated to assert saved-then-released, without deleting it. No test touches a real worktree under ~/Code/.reckon-worktrees. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Let a finished worktree save its residue in its run directory and release without a forced removal, as a-finished-worktree-releases-without-a-force §3 states.
